hypotheses.text: The primary clinical discriminators differentiating LRRC7-related neurodevelopmental disorder from other postsynaptic density synaptopathies (e.g., SYNGAP1, SHANK3, DLG4) are the prominent presence of severe aggressive behavior and hyperphagia-associated obesity, rather than the absence of seizures or hypotonia.
hypotheses.rationale: Prior diagnostic frameworks relied on an assumed absence of hypotonia or seizures to rule out SYNGAP1 or SHANK3 in favor of LRRC7. However, the landmark cohort study and subsequent literature establish that LRRC7-related disorder does manifest hypotonia and seizures, while uniquely featuring a prominent behavioral profile of marked aggression and hyperphagia-associated obesity among PSD scaffold disorders.

evidence.text: In the definitive cohort of 33 individuals with dominant LRRC7 variants, the phenotypic spectrum is defined by intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, aggression, and in several cases, hyperphagia-associated obesity.

hypotheses.text: Seizures are a recurrent finding in approximately 18% to 25% of individuals with LRRC7-related disorder and typically present as responsive absence or tonic seizures, contrasting sharply with the near-universal (>80%) and pharmaco-resistant epilepsy that characterizes SYNGAP1-related encephalopathy.
hypotheses.rationale: Tests of whether epilepsy discriminates between LRRC7 and other channelopathies/synaptopathies must clarify that epilepsy is not absent in LRRC7, but has a significantly lower penetrance and milder course than in SYNGAP1.

evidence.text: Across reported LRRC7 cases, seizures are observed in approximately 18% of the cohort, as demonstrated by literature synthesis and a newly reported proband with tonic seizures.

hypotheses.text: Hypotonia and mild microcephaly are present in approximately 30% to 50% of individuals with LRRC7 variants, proving that the mere presence of hypotonia cannot be used as an exclusion criterion to differentiate LRRC7-related disorder from SHANK3 deficiency (Phelan-McDermid syndrome).
hypotheses.rationale: Previous assertions suggested distinguishing LRRC7 from SHANK3 based on the absence of hypotonia. Emerging cohort data contradict this assumption by documenting hypotonia and microcephaly in roughly one-third of LRRC7-affected individuals.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance, age of onset, and satiety profile of hyperphagia and obesity in the 33-patient LRRC7 cohort compared to classic hyperphagic genetic disorders (e.g., Prader-Willi, SIM1, MC4R)?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the specific quantitative prevalence and clinical onset of hyperphagia/obesity in the n=33 cohort would determine how reliably hyperphagia can serve as a phenotypic hallmark distinguishing LRRC7 from other synaptic scaffold disorders.

new_directions.question_text: How do electroclinical features and response to anti-seizure medications in LRRC7-associated seizures compare systematically with those of SYNGAP1 and GRIN2B?
new_directions.rationale: Resolving seizure semiology, pharmacoresponsiveness, and EEG patterns in LRRC7 will enable clinicians to distinguish LRRC7 from other synaptopathies when seizures are present.
